plan: This ascending clock auction with sealed exit bids functions as a second-price auction: I win if my bid is highest, and I pay the second-highest bid, not my own. Therefore, bidding my true value ($25) is the dominant strategy—it maximizes expected profit since I only pay less than my bid when I win, and bidding higher or lower than true value only risks either overpaying or losing profitable opportunities. No history exists to suggest otherwise.

This is structurally a second-price auction: my sealed bid acts as my exit price in the ascending clock, and I pay the price at which the auction ends (determined by the second-highest bid). Bidding my true value ($3) is the dominant strategy - if I win, I pay less than my value (profit), and if I lose, someone else valued it more. Bidding above or below true value only risks losing profitable trades or overpaying. I'll bid exactly $3.

Since this is essentially a second-price auction (the winner pays the second-highest bid, determined by the ascending clock mechanism), the dominant strategy is to bid my true value. Bidding higher than my value risks paying more than the item is worth, and bidding lower risks losing an auction I could have profitably won. With my value at $26, I will bid exactly $26 to maximize expected profit.
